text.arabic_uthmani: قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى ۚ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌۭ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍۢ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

words.gloss_range: completed speech act introducing Joseph's formal counterclaim
words.root_gloss_range: saying, assertion, and propositional speech; locally narrowed to a public rebuttal placed on record
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) opens with Joseph's completed counter-speech, not a private aside: the omitted addressee lets the rebuttal face the whole household scene. Its perfect active form puts Joseph personally on record after the feminine accusation of 12:25, and the word launches a sequence in which assertion is followed by witness, condition, and verdict (12:25-28; 12:51).

topics.headline: public completed rebuttal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph's first word is a formal counterclaim placed before the scene, not merely a line of dialogue.
topics.reason: The perfect speech verb governs only Joseph's short quoted defense, while the absent addressee and legal scene make the utterance public-facing.

topics.headline: assertion enters proof sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah shifting from speech to testimony and then to conditional proof.
topics.reason: The q-w-l opening is followed by sh-h-d testimony and the conditional shirt test, so it functions as the first evidentiary channel rather than neutral narration.

topics.headline: gendered turn-taking echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the turn from the woman's accusation in 12:25 to Joseph's answer in 12:26 through the repeated speech root with changed gender.
topics.reason: The same q-w-l speech frame crosses the 12:25-12:26 boundary, reversing speaker gender and discourse role.

words.gloss_range: fronted independent feminine pronoun identifying the actor before the verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:هِيَ}} ({{tr:hiya}}) stands separately before the verb even though the following form already marks a feminine subject. That fronting makes identity the first point of Joseph's defense: she, not he, initiated the action. The pronoun also begins a she/he frame that closes with {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) later in the verdict clause.

topics.headline: emphatic actor identification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counterclaim starts by isolating the actor before naming the act.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun is syntactically tied to the following verb but is retained as a separate fronted subject for contrastive identification.

topics.headline: she/he dispute bookend
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is framed as a two-party dispute, opening with her identity and closing with his conditional classification.
topics.reason: The opening feminine pronoun and later masculine pronoun create a visible identity frame around the evidentiary middle.

words.gloss_range: Form III completed solicitation directed at Joseph with a first-person object suffix
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, repeated approach, solicitation, and negotiation; locally narrowed to persistent attempted seduction/diversion

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:رَاوَدَتْنِي}} ({{tr:rāwadatnī}}) carries the countercharge itself: the feminine subject and first-person object make her the initiator and Joseph the affected party. Form III and the following {{ar:عَنْ نَفْسِي}} ({{tr:ʿan nafsī}}) make the action sustained pressure away from his own self, not a neutral wish. The same r-w-d field links the private event of 12:23, the accusation of 12:25, and the later confession in 12:51.

topics.headline: persistent pressure against the self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph describes pressure designed to draw him away from himself, not merely attraction toward another person.
topics.reason: The Form III verb, first-person object suffix, and governed self phrase together select persistent solicitation against resistance.

topics.headline: agency assigned to her
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the accusation reversed at the level of grammar: she is agent, Joseph is object.
topics.reason: The feminine verbal marking and fronted pronoun assign agency to the wife while the bound object suffix assigns affectedness to Joseph.

topics.headline: seduction formula chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this word as part of a repeated disclosure formula across the seduction arc (12:23; 12:26; 12:51).
topics.reason: The r-w-d recurrence moves from narrated seduction to first-person countercharge and then to confession, so the word is not isolated.

words.gloss_range: preposition selecting separation from the self in this construction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation
nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) is the vector word in Joseph's phrase. Its broader range can include topical or causal senses, but with {{ar:رَاوَدَتْنِي}} ({{tr:rāwadatnī}}) and {{ar:نَفْسِي}} ({{tr:nafsī}}) the local force is separation: she sought to divert him away from his self. The short preposition depends on the following noun, so the moral direction is completed only by the two-word unit.

topics.headline: away-from-self vector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the seduction is framed as movement away from Joseph's self, not merely persuasion about him.
topics.reason: The topical and causal possibilities of the preposition are narrowed by the verb plus governed self-noun into an ablative separation reading.

topics.headline: preposition completed by self noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause remains incomplete until the self phrase supplies the direction of the attempted diversion.
topics.reason: The preposition immediately governs the next word and structurally completes the seduction vector.

words.gloss_range: Joseph's possessed self as the point from which diversion is attempted
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, person, desire, will, and breath-life; locally moral selfhood with embodied inward pressure
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسِي}} ({{tr:nafsī}}) closes Joseph's direct speech on self-possession. The first-person suffix makes the contested self his own, while the n-f-s range keeps desire and resistance simultaneously in view: the self is temptable, yet it is also the place from which refusal holds. The formula returns when the wife later confesses the same r-w-d plus self construction in 12:51.

topics.headline: personal moral possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attempted diversion targets Joseph's own moral self, not an abstract or detachable object.
topics.reason: The genitive governed noun with first-person suffix makes the self both grammatically dependent on the preposition and personally owned by Joseph.

topics.headline: temptable yet resisting self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the inward tension: the self is the site of appetite and the site of resistance.
topics.reason: The local phrase selects moral selfhood while preserving the root-family pressure of desire, will, and living inwardness.

topics.headline: self formula returns in confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph's wording anticipates the later confession using the same solicitation-self formula (12:51).
topics.reason: The same r-w-d plus n-f-s construction recurs in 12:51 with reversed speaker, turning this phrase into a legal refrain.

words.gloss_range: conjunction resuming narration into the witness clause after Joseph's speech

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links Joseph's completed counterclaim to the witness clause while opening a new narrated beat. The connector preserves continuity, but the clause boundary matters: the witness is not simply folded into Joseph's own quoted speech. The fused surface before {{ar:شَهِدَ}} ({{tr:shahida}}) makes the transition into testimony immediate.

topics.headline: continuity without quote collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that testimony follows Joseph's claim as connected evidence while remaining a separate narrated intervention.
topics.reason: Scope evidence ends the quote at the self phrase, while the conjunction links the next narrated testimony clause to it.

topics.headline: not embedded in Joseph's quote
topics.blocking_evidence: Attachment clause evidence marks words 2-5 as the quoted complement of the speech verb and words 6-10 as a separate testimony clause.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence confines Joseph's direct speech to words 2-5 and marks words 6-10 as a separate testimony clause.

words.gloss_range: completed act of testimony introducing the evidentiary procedure
words.root_gloss_range: being present, witnessing, and testifying; locally formal attestation grounded in presence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:شَهِدَ}} ({{tr:shahida}}) moves the scene from counterclaim to attestation. The perfect verb reports a completed witness act, and the same-root subject {{ar:شَاهِدٌ}} ({{tr:shāhidun}}) gives the testimony clause a compact double weight. Compared with broader witness scenes and titles (11:17; 13:43; 17:96), the local sh-h-d field remains domestic and household-forensic, while the same witness language returns within Surah 12 at 12:81.

topics.headline: claim becomes evidence procedure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the epistemic shift from Joseph's assertion to witnessed certification.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I testimony verb stands after the speech claim and before the conditional test, making it the pivot into procedure.

topics.headline: verb and witness reinforce each other
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears act and agent doubled in the adjacent same-root construction.
topics.reason: The verb is immediately followed by an active-participle subject from the same root, tightening the testimony clause.

topics.headline: domestic witness within wider witness language
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this domestic witness as part of a broader Surah 12 testimony pattern, while the local scene remains household-forensic (12:26; 12:81).
topics.reason: Broader sh-h-d registers are relevant as contrast and echo, but local syntax selects a human witness act in this domestic proof scene.

words.gloss_range: indefinite active-participle witness, later specified as from her household
words.root_gloss_range: witness, attestor, present one, and evidentiary sign; locally an unnamed human attestor with material-sign resonance

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:شَاهِدٌ}} ({{tr:shāhidun}}) is an unnamed active witness, not an abstract testimony noun. Its indefiniteness withholds biography until {{ar:مِنْ أَهْلِهَا}} ({{tr:min ahlihā}}) supplies the decisive credential: the attestor comes from her side. Because the shirt itself will bear the decisive mark, the word also keeps a controlled witness/sign layering without replacing the human witness.

topics.headline: one unnamed attestor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an unnamed single witness is enough because the procedure, not celebrity identity, carries the proof.
topics.reason: The nominative indefinite active participle is the subject of the testimony verb and remains unidentified until the source phrase.

topics.headline: human witness with sign resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a layered evidentiary setup: a human witness speaks, while the shirt functions as the material sign read by that testimony.
topics.reason: The active attestor is selected by the following conditional speech, while the semantic range of sign remains relevant because the shirt supplies the decisive trace.

topics.headline: witness narrowed by source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the delayed turn from anonymous witness to insider witness.
topics.reason: The noun is immediately followed by the source phrase, so its credibility is completed by household affiliation.

words.gloss_range: source/partitive preposition attaching the witness to her household

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) turns the anonymous {{ar:شَاهِدٌ}} ({{tr:shāhidun}}) into someone from among her household. The preposition is small but load-bearing: it makes social origin a grammatical credential, first leaving the witness unnamed and then binding him to her side.

topics.headline: from-among household credential
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness's credibility comes through insider source membership, not through a named public office.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the household noun and modifies the witness, selecting partitive-source membership.

words.gloss_range: her household or kin as the source group of the witness
words.root_gloss_range: belonging, household, people, kin, and qualified group; locally her domestic kin group
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلِهَا}} ({{tr:ahlihā}}) makes the witness socially internal to the woman Joseph just identified. The suffix reaches back to her, so the testimony does not arrive from a neutral outsider; it comes from her household and can therefore overturn partisan expectation. Public min-ahl affiliation formulas such as 12:109 remain contrastive; here the phrase is narrowed to domestic kinship and evidentiary proximity.

topics.headline: insider source against expectation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof gains force because the witness comes from the accuser's own side.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix resolves to the woman and makes household affiliation the witness's credibility credential.

topics.headline: household rather than public peoplehood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ahl is not a generic public peoplehood term here; it contracts to her domestic circle.
topics.reason: The possessed noun under the source preposition selects concrete household kin, while broader qualification or town-affiliation uses remain contrastive.

topics.headline: household language shifts role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices household language shifting from the wife's accusation context in 12:25 to the source of testimony in 12:26.
topics.reason: The suffix and repeated household field carry the previous scene into the witness source, changing household from alleged victim-context to evidentiary source.

words.gloss_range: real conditional particle opening the verifiable shirt test
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) opens a real, checkable condition: the shirt is present, so the test can be inspected rather than imagined. This is the first branch only, the front-tear branch; 12:27 supplies the matching back-tear branch and completes the binary proof system.

topics.headline: inspectable if-test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness turns the case into a material test that can actually be checked.
topics.reason: The particle introduces a real protasis over the garment state rather than an unreal counterfactual.

topics.headline: front branch awaiting back branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this ayah states only one half of the proof, with the matching branch delayed to 12:27.
topics.reason: The protasis-answer structure in 12:26 is mirrored by 12:27, so the particle begins a two-branch forensic test.

words.gloss_range: conditional copula making the shirt's state the evidence variable
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, and state; locally narrowed to an examinable garment-state copula

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) sits under the conditional, so its perfect form functions as an inspectable state: if the shirt is found to be in this torn condition. The broad being-verb is narrowed to a forensic copula linking {{ar:قَمِيصُهُ}} ({{tr:qamīṣuhu}}) with the torn-state predicate, and the same frame is repeated in 12:27 with the opposite direction.

topics.headline: being narrowed to state test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the broad being verb becomes a concrete inspection frame for the garment.
topics.reason: The conditional and shirt predicate narrow k-w-n from broad existence to a verifiable state relation.

topics.headline: state controls verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict is licensed by the shirt's state rather than by either party's assertion.
topics.reason: The copula takes the shirt as subject and the passive torn phrase as predicate, so the material state governs the answer clause.

topics.headline: same frame repeated in 12:27
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proof formula repeating across 12:26-27, with direction alone changing the verdict.
topics.reason: The in-kāna frame recurs in the next ayah, making two directions operate inside one proof design.

words.gloss_range: his specific shirt as the material exhibit in the condition
words.root_gloss_range: shirt or tunic as close-body garment; locally a contact-record and proof object

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:قَمِيصُهُ}} ({{tr:qamīṣuhu}}) is the concrete exhibit. The suffix makes it Joseph's specific shirt, while its position as the subject of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) makes the garment, not the rival speeches, carry the proof. The qamīṣ motif is confined to Surah 12, where shirts bear false blood, tear direction, and later recognition (12:18; 12:25-28; 12:93).

topics.headline: his shirt as inspectable proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one specific garment becomes the evidentiary object that can classify a person.
topics.reason: The possessed singular noun is the subject of the condition and bears the state on which the verdict depends.

topics.headline: body-adjacent cloth records motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shirt as a close-body surface that preserves contact traces, not merely as clothing.
topics.reason: The garment semantics and clause role make the shirt a material record between accusation and truth-verdict.

topics.headline: Surah 12 shirt motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the shirt is a Surah 12 motif moving from false evidence to trial evidence to later recognition (12:18; 12:26-28; 12:93).
topics.reason: The q-m-s lexeme is restricted to Surah 12 in the supplied evidence and recurs at narrative turning points.

words.gloss_range: passive perfect torn/split verb, despite the particle-like surface risk
words.root_gloss_range: cutting, splitting, or tearing; locally a completed passive tear whose direction can be inspected
words.prose: {{ar:قُدَّ}} ({{tr:qudda}}) must be read as the rare passive torn verb, not as the certitude particle. Its passive perfect suppresses the tearing agent and leaves an inspectable result: a completed split whose direction can be measured by the following phrase. The root moves from active narration in 12:25 to passive proof condition here and in 12:27-28.

topics.headline: agent suppressed, result inspected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof rests on an inspectable tear result, not on a narrated tearing agent.
topics.reason: The passive perfect places the completed torn state in the predicate of the conditional test.

topics.headline: torn verb recovered from tag mismatch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a visually particle-like form is actually the rare verbal tear pivot of the proof.
topics.reason: The bundle explicitly warns that the MASAQ particle tag is misleading; root and gloss evidence identify the passive q-d-d verb.

topics.headline: linear tear becomes legal criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the line of rupture turns cloth damage into a directional criterion for guilt or innocence.
topics.reason: The tear verb is completed by a directional phrase, and the same q-d-d proof frame continues through 12:27-28.

words.gloss_range: spatial-origin preposition marking the front side as the tear source

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the tear directional. It governs {{ar:قُبُلٍ}} ({{tr:qubulin}}) as the origin side of the rupture, so the shirt is not merely damaged; it is damaged from a readable direction. Because 12:25 already told the reader the tear was from behind, this front-origin branch is heard as the condition that will fail.

topics.headline: front as governed origin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns damage into a spatial vector that can decide the case.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the front noun and attaches to the passive tear, completing the predicate with origin direction.

topics.headline: known back-tear shadows front branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices dramatic irony: the front branch is stated even though 12:25 has already supplied the back-tear fact.
topics.reason: The prior narrative evidence in 12:25 makes the current front-origin hypothesis contrastive rather than neutral.

words.gloss_range: front-facing side of the shirt in the first proof branch
words.root_gloss_range: facing, frontness, receiving, accepting, before-ness, and orientation; locally physical front direction
words.prose: {{ar:قُبُلٍ}} ({{tr:qubulin}}) is the front term in the proof. The broad q-b-l field of facing, receiving, and before-ness is narrowed by the torn-shirt condition to physical front direction; it is not an independent body-part claim. Accepted case variants expose how tightly the word is tied to direction, but the standard governed reading keeps it as the front side that maps to the she-true/he-liar branch before 12:27 gives the back-side answer.

topics.headline: frontness as forensic direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that frontness is not descriptive scenery; it is the spatial condition that would decide the verdict.
topics.reason: The q-b-l semantic range is narrowed by q-d-d and min to physical front direction inside the proof.

topics.headline: variant readings expose syntactic pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant case readings make the front-direction word a syntactic pressure point, while the local standard still governs it by the preposition.
topics.reason: The variants can show complement or adverbial pressure, but the local canonical form remains genitive after the preposition.

topics.headline: direction maps to truth classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proof system: front/back direction maps onto truth/falsehood classification across 12:26-27.
topics.reason: The front word is half of an antonymic pair with the back term in 12:27, and the verdict terms give that spatial pair moral force.

words.gloss_range: answer-particle joining the condition to its immediate verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge where inspection becomes verdict. As the answer-particle of the condition, it makes the front-tear state immediately entail {{ar:صَدَقَتْ}} ({{tr:ṣadaqat}}); the proof does not pause for a separate argument. The small proclitic fuses logical consequence to the truth verb.

topics.headline: proof-to-verdict entailment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact point where physical evidence is converted into a legal verdict.
topics.reason: The particle marks the jawāb of the protasis and creates immediate logical consequence.

topics.headline: proclitic fused to truth verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict arrives as one tightly joined consequent form, not as a loose next statement.
topics.reason: The written proclitic attaches directly to the truth verb and sits at the structural pivot of the condition.

words.gloss_range: she proved truthful under the front-tear condition
words.root_gloss_range: truth, correspondence, sincerity, confirmation, and truthful character; locally a conditional truth-verdict on her claim
words.prose: {{ar:صَدَقَتْ}} ({{tr:ṣadaqat}}) returns the verdict to the woman through the feminine perfect ending. It is a conditional truth finding, not a general character certificate: if the front tear were found, her claim would align with the material evidence. The word also forms the first half of the truth/falsehood axis that reverses in 12:27 and echoes through the Surah 12 truth chain (12:17; 12:51; 12:111).

topics.headline: claim verified, character not certified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness verifies a claim under a condition rather than praising the woman's whole character.
topics.reason: The fa-answer and shirt condition narrow the truth root to a verdict on the claim, while the verbal form avoids stable adjective-of-character force.

topics.headline: verdict returns to her
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar routing the verdict back across the evidence clause to the woman named at the start.
topics.reason: The feminine perfect ending resolves to the earlier feminine pronoun and precedes the coordinated male liar classification.

topics.headline: truth term mirrors falsehood class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this truth verdict is half of a mirrored truth/falsehood system completed in 12:27.
topics.reason: The s-d-q term pairs locally with the k-dh-b class and reverses in the next proof branch.

words.gloss_range: connector joining or circumstantially pairing the male liar clause with her truth verdict
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) attaches the second verdict to the first. It can be read as coordination and also permits a circumstantial coloring: if she is truthful, he is in that same case among the liars. The separate connector preserves a clause boundary while balancing a verbal truth verdict with a nominal classification.

topics.headline: two verdicts jointly asserted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that her truth and his liar-status are not independent events but paired consequences of the same condition.
topics.reason: The connector links the verbal and nominal verdict clauses under one conditional branch.

topics.headline: distinct second verdict clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second classification as a distinct clause while still simultaneous with the first verdict.
topics.reason: The separate particle before the independent pronoun keeps the nominal clause visible and allows circumstantial simultaneity.

words.gloss_range: explicit independent masculine pronoun fixing the classified party

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to preserve the local syntactic or evidentiary relation

words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) fixes the male party before the liar predicate. The pronoun links the verdict to Joseph, the same referent attached to the shirt by the possessive suffix, and mirrors the opening {{ar:هِيَ}} ({{tr:hiya}}). The ayah thus begins with her identified as actor and ends this branch with him conditionally classified.

topics.headline: male party fixed before predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the liar predicate is anchored to one male referent, not left as an impersonal class statement.
topics.reason: The independent masculine singular pronoun is the subject of the final prepositional predicate and resolves to Joseph.

topics.headline: pronoun ring frames dispute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a she/he frame around the whole evidentiary middle of the ayah.
topics.reason: The opening feminine pronoun and closing masculine pronoun map the two disputants onto accusation and conditional classification.

words.gloss_range: partitive/classificatory preposition placing him among the liar class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) turns the predicate into membership: he would be among the liars. With the definite plural that follows, the preposition does more than attach an adjective; it places the subject inside a class and completes the final nominal verdict.

topics.headline: among the liars
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict assigns class membership rather than merely describing one false statement.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the definite plural active participle and supplies the predicate of the independent pronoun.

topics.headline: prepositional verdict closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's first proof branch closes structurally in the prepositional predicate.
topics.reason: The min phrase completes the final nominal clause of the branch.

words.gloss_range: definite plural active-participle liar class at the close of the branch
words.root_gloss_range: lying, denial, false accusation, and falsehood; locally classifying a person among false agents under the condition
words.prose: {{ar:الْكَاذِبِينَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibīn}}) closes the ayah on class membership. The definite plural active participle makes him, under the front-tear hypothesis, one of the liar class rather than merely the speaker of one mistaken sentence; yet it is not the strongest intensive liar pattern. This final word seals the first half of the truth/falsehood axis that 12:27 reverses with the opposite class. Its testimony/falsehood formula also resonates with other evidentiary settings (9:107; 24:8; 27:27), while the local scene remains Joseph's household trial.

topics.headline: known class membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict places the accused inside an identifiable class of liars.
topics.reason: The definite genitive plural under the preposition creates a membership predicate rather than a simple adjective.

topics.headline: active participle without maximal intensification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a person-class verdict, while the form stops short of selecting the strongest habitual-liar pattern.
topics.reason: The active participle classifies a false agent, but the absence of an intensive pattern limits overstatement.

topics.headline: final half of mirrored axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing liar class as only the first half of a mirrored truth/falsehood system completed in 12:27.
topics.reason: The final k-dh-b term pairs with the truth verb here and is answered by the opposite class in the next ayah.

topics.headline: falsehood sorted by testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local domestic verdict belongs to a wider testimony/falsehood formula field (9:107; 24:8), while the local scene remains Joseph's household trial.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The witness's conditional joins the shirt, its longitudinal tear, its front orientation, and the opposed truth labels.
baseline_models.mechanism: A worn covering becomes a trace surface: the direction of its damage mediates between incompatible spoken accounts.

activation_trace.role: The mark-as-witness branch lets a visible trace carry testimony beyond the human speaker.
The worn covering supplies the physical surface attached to the body and its movement.
The longitudinal slit makes the damage directional rather than generic.
Front-facing orientation supplies the spatial variable tested by the conditional.
Truth of speech is the positive verdict assigned when the material condition holds.
Contradiction of truth supplies the opposed verdict, making the test discriminative.

changed_reading.before: A witness verbally decides which claimant is truthful.
changed_reading.after: The witness proposes a material cross-examination in which the garment's oriented damage is made to testify.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The clause begins with a condition about whether the shirt is torn from the front before assigning truth and falsehood.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah suspends judgment inside a possible state of affairs; truth status is downstream of an inspectable spatial condition, not of rank or first accusation.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence in a state or time frames the proposed tear pattern as a condition to be established.
Knowledge-based clarification makes testimony a reasoned test rather than an unsupported preference.
Priority and forward orientation keep open one hypothesized ordering of the encounter.
Her truth is explicitly conditional rather than presumed.
Attribution of lying is likewise produced by the test instead of attached to him in advance.

changed_reading.before: Yusuf's denial simply counters her accusation with another assertion.
changed_reading.after: The ayah interrupts assertion with a falsifiable hypothesis, temporarily withholding the social labels of truthful and liar.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Yusuf says that she solicited him away from or concerning his own self, while clarification comes from one of her own people.
baseline_models.mechanism: A struggle over another's will is answered by first-person self-assertion, then tested by a voice arising inside the accuser's affiliation.

activation_trace.role: Audible speech lets Yusuf reclaim grammatical agency by naming her as the acting party.
Solicitation as a contest of wills makes the dispute concern pressure on another's chosen action.
The thing-itself branch anchors the pressure in Yusuf's own person rather than an abstract temptation.
The inner awareness branch opens an autonomy reading in which his inward judgment is under pressure.
Near affiliation makes the corrective witness socially internal to her side.

changed_reading.before: He reports an attempted seduction, and a convenient witness happens to be present.
changed_reading.after: He asserts self-command against an attempt to redirect his will, and her own affiliation generates an internal check on her account.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier chain of concealment, commodification, undervalued exchange, purchase, and proposed adoption gives the focus phrase about his own self a history of other people assigning uses and identities to him.

activation_trace.role: His own person is the focus anchor against which prior acts of appropriation are reread.
Concealment places Yusuf inside a hidden transaction before he can speak for himself.
A tradable portion converts the concealed person into merchandise.
Exchange supplies the explicit transfer through which others dispose of him.
Diminution of due worth intensifies the reduction of a person to an undervalued object.
Taking or acquiring as a son assigns a new household identity from outside.

structural_cues: 12:19-12:21 orders the sequence as concealment, merchandise, sale, purchase, and possible adoption before the focus dispute.
The focus is the first line in this window where Yusuf's first-person speech explicitly centers his own self.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated external disposal of Yusuf; I infer that 'my self' can reassert self-possession against that history. A live alternative is that the earlier chain is narrative background and the phrase remains only the ordinary idiom of solicitation.

changed_reading.before: The phrase describes only the immediate object of sexual solicitation.
changed_reading.after: Without losing that sense, it can also mark Yusuf's reassertion of personhood after a sequence in which others hid, priced, transferred, and reassigned him.

context_deltas.mechanism: Closed access, direct summons, active self-protection, command, and threatened confinement turn the focus solicitation into a pressure system backed by control of space and punishment.

summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah converts an oriented tear into conditional testimony while preserving several scales at once: bodily agency, household affiliation, public reputation, material inference, and the later gap between recognized truth and exercised power.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه راد الكلأ وارتاده بمعنى طلبه، والرائد المرسل أو الطالب للكلإ، والرجل الرأد بمعنى الرائد.
يدخل فيه راد الشيء إذا جاء وذهب، ورياد الإبل واختلافها في المرعى، والمراد موضع التردد، ورادت المرأة إلى بيوت جاراتها، وراد وساده إذا لم يستقر.
يدخل فيه أرود في السير إذا رفق، والمشي على رود، ورويد ورويدك بمعنى مهلا وأمهل، والرادة من الرياح السهلة التي لا تهب بشدة.
يدخل فيه الرائد بمعنى يد الرحى أو العود الذي تدار به، والمرود بمعنى الميل والحديدة التي تدور في اللجام ومحور البكرة من حديد.
يدخل فيه رائد العين، أي عوارها الذي يرود فيها.
يدخل فيه جارية رود بمعنى شابة، ومعها الرؤدة والرأدة بالهمز في الصحاح بمعنى الشابة الحسنة.

يدخل فيه طلب رد الشيء واسترجاع المتاع، وتراد المتبايعين من الرد والفسخ
يدخل فيه رجوع المرء من الإسلام إلى الكفر، والردة اسما لذلك، والمرتد

يدخل فيه الشاة أو الناقة إذا أضرعت أو امتلأ ضرعها، وكثرة الماء أو الموج، واجتماع ماء الرجل بطول العزبة

يدخل فيه نفس الله الكربة، والتنفس عن المكروب، والفرج من الشدة، والريح أو الأنصار حين تذكر باعتبار التفريج.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تسمية العين نفسا، وإصابة المنظور بنفس، والنافس بمعنى العائن.
يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الدم، والنفس السائلة، وتسميته نفسا لأن فقد الدم يذهب بالنفس.
يدخل فيه النفاس ولادة المرأة، والنفساء، والمنفوس بمعنى المولود، واستعماله في الحيض حيث نص المصدر عليه.
يدخل فيه الشرب بنفس أو أنفاس، والنفس بمعنى الجرعة أو المستراح في الشرب.
يدخل فيه النفس أو النفسين من الدباغ، أي مقدار يسير يدبغ به الجلد مرة أو مرتين.
يدخل فيه تسمية الماء نفسا، والشراب ذو النفس إذا كان فيه سعة وري، ونقيضه الشراب غير ذي نفس.
يدخل فيه تنفس الصبح والنهار إذا تبلج أو امتد، وتنفس القوس إذا انشقت، وزيادة الماء أو الموج حين يخرجان أو ينتشران.
يدخل فيه النفيس والنفاسة والمنفس، والرغبة والمنافسة في الشيء، والضن أو الحسد به إذا كان لقيمته ورغبة النفس فيه.
يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الروح والحياة، وكل إنسان نفس، وخروج النفس عند الموت، والنفس الحية التي بها حياة الجسد.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه التأهل والتزوج، وأهل الرجل أو أهل امرأة، والدعاء بآهلك الله في الجنة أي زوجك فيها وجعل لك أهلا.
يدخل فيه فلان أهل لكذا أو خليق به، وأهل التقوى والمغفرة، وتأهيل الشخص لأمر.
يدخل فيه المكان المأهول أو الآهل، وكون الشيء أو الدابة يألف مكانا فيكون أهليا، والأنس بالإنسان أو المكان.
يدخل فيه قول مرحبا وأهلا في التحية، بمعنى وجدت سعة وأتيت أهلا لا غرباء فاستأنس ولا تستوحش.
يدخل فيه الإهالة: الألية أو الودك أو الشحم أو الزيت وما يؤتدم به، وما يعلو القدر من ودك اللحم السمين، واستأهل بمعنى أخذ الإهالة أو أكلها أو ائتدم بها.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın yön ve ön taraf anlamını korur; yüz yüze yapma, karşısında bulunma ve yönsüz kalma gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımları ayrı yüzeyler olarak tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başka bir şeye dönük, onun karşısında ya da yüz yüze bulunması ve bu ilişki içinde belirlenen ön taraf veya yöndür. Karşıdan görülen yamaç ile doğrudan görerek yapma, bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: İki şey birbirine dönüktür ve karşı karşıya bulunur.
Bir şeyin ön tarafı, arka tarafının karşıtı olarak bu yön ilişkisiyle belirlenir.
Bir işi yüz yüze ve doğrudan görerek yapmak, karşı karşıyalığın eylem bağlamındaki kullanımıdır.
Dağın ya da arazinin bakana dönük yüzü, yön çekirdeğinin yer biçimlerine uygulanmasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar karşı karşıya bulunma, önün arkaya karşıt oluşu ve doğrudan görüş altında yapma anlamlarında birleşir; yer şeklinin bakana dönük yüzü de aynı yön düzenine bağlanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin sonrakine göre önce gelmesini ve henüz gelmemiş yıl ya da gecenin yaklaşmasını aynı öncelik düzeninde toplar. Gençliğin başlangıcı da bu düzenin yaşam evresine uygulanmasıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel önce ve sonra karşıtlığını korur; gelecek yıl, bundan sonrası ve gençliğin başlangıcı gibi biçime ya da kalıba bağlı kullanımları buna karıştırmadan belirtir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin zaman, yer, sıra veya düzey bakımından başka bir şeyden önce bulunmasıdır. Yaklaşan yıl ya da gece ile bir yaşam evresinin başlangıcı, bu öncelik çizgisinin ileriye dönük özel kullanımlarıdır.

facets.statement: Bir şey, zaman, yer, sıra veya düzey bakımından sonrakinin önünde bulunur.
Henüz gelmemiş yıl veya gece, yaklaşan ve sırada olan dönem diye belirtilir.
Gençliğin ilk evresi, yaşlılık belirtisi henüz görünmeden önceki başlangıç dönemi olarak anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar önce ile sonra arasındaki karşıtlığı temel alır ve bu ilişkiyi yaklaşan dönemlere, gelecekteki zamana ve gençliğin ilk evresine uygular.

يدخل فيه القابلة التي تتلقى الولد عند الولادة والقابل الذي يستقبل دلو السانية أو الغرب من المستقي
يدخل فيه القبيل الكفيل والقبالة والكفالة وتقبل فلان بغيره والعهد المكتوب

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı yalanın karşıtı olan söz doğruluğu olarak kurar ve daha özel olarak sözün hem konuşanın iç inancına hem de anlattığı gerçeğe uymasını ister. Bu nedenle dal, genel doğruluk kavramına genişletilmeden söz ve bildirim alanında tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimdeki söz doğruluğunu temel alır; konuşmada doğruyu söyleme ve bir sözün doğruluğunu kabul etme gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımları ayrıca sınırlar.
